result.reason: Clarity: A is sectioned with plain-English headers and defines each technical term as it appears (current yield, duration, and a simple one-sentence explanation of what a call date is and why it prompted the sale) — satisfying the tone note to explain call risk once, simply. B is four undifferentiated blocks that leave 'fixed-to-floating,' 'duration to worst' and '$25 par value' unexplained, never explains call risk at all, presents performance figures out of order (quarter, gross, benchmark, since-inception, then back to YTD), and fuses the sale with the duration cut so the reasoning for the trade reads as muddier than it is. Tone: closer, but still A. A is warm and unintrusive — 'call me any time,' 'Warm regards' — with one slip in addressing the letter to her 'and family' when the IRA is hers alone after a spousal rollover. B earns warmth with the concrete nod to the income she relies on monthly, but closes with 'as you navigate this important chapter of your life,' a vague euphemism for her bereavement that is neither warm nor plain and reads as presumptuous, compounded by the first-name salutation. A's error is a minor misaddress; B's is unearned intimacy about a recent loss. Overall A, comfortably, on ease of reading and fit to this client.
